sections: 23.6 Schema, datasource, runtime, and internal failures

observations: The retained critical contract mutations for code, phase, source kind, symbol argument, span, generated location and guidance were all killed by their nominated tests.
Independent REC-145 challengers killed an enum composite-name mutation, a warning-code mutation, a cancellation-token identity mutation and a state-reuse leakage mutation.
The equivalent control remained equivalent, the invalid assertion API was classified compilation-invalid, and the timeout probe was classified timeout rather than killed.
The mutation script used a detached temporary worktree, reset it before every mutant and removed it in a finally block; the main checkout retained no production mutant.

obligations.result: The final mutation map covers wrong code, phase, source kind, argument, span, generated location, guidance action, cancellation identity, state-reuse leakage, enum behavior and warning behavior; every critical mutant was killed.
All 13 mutants ran in a detached temporary worktree that was reset before each mutation and removed after the run; no production mutant remained in the campaign checkout.
The nominated assertion failed for all 11 critical mutants; the equivalent and compilation-invalid controls were classified separately, with no survivor or timeout.
REC-145-M01 and REC-145-M02 independently challenge enum composite-name and warning-code paths, and both were killed by their nominated tests.

The mutation worktree was removed and the main checkout had no production mutant; the fresh clean unmutated Release gate passed 21,065 tests with 0 failures and 3 established refresh skips across all 8 targets.

boundaries: The raw mutation receipt is retained under ignored campaign artifacts and is not committed as source; its digest is recorded here.
No intentionally broken production mutant was committed.
No production fix was required and no installed provider, CLI, profile, credential or user state was used.
